sentences.zh: :儒者，所以助人君明教化者也。

translations.literal: Confucians are those who help the ruler clarify and transform the people.
translations.idiomatic: Confucians are those who help the ruler clarify and transform the people.

sentences.zh: 聖人之教，非家至而戶說，故有儒者宣而明之。

translations.literal: The teaching of the sages does not reach every household in person, and therefore there are Confucians who proclaim and clarify it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the sages could not visit every home in person, Confucians arose to proclaim and clarify their teaching.

sentences.zh: 其大抵本于仁義及五常之道，黃帝、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，鹹由此則。

translations.literal: Its general purport rests on benevolence, righteousness, and the Way of the Five Constants; the Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu all followed this path.
translations.idiomatic: At its core it rests on benevolence, righteousness, and the Way of the Five Constants—the path followed by the Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu alike.

sentences.zh: 《周官》：太宰以九兩系邦國之人，其四曰儒是也。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou states that the Grand Steward employs the nine categories of bond to attach the people of the state to the court, and the fourth category is the Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou states that the Grand Steward employs nine categories of bond to attach the people of the state to the court, and the fourth category is the Confucian.

sentences.zh: 其後陵夷衰亂，儒道廢闕。

translations.literal: Afterward it declined into disorder and the Confucian Way was abandoned and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the age declined into disorder, and the Confucian Way was abandoned and cut off.

sentences.zh: 仲尼祖述前代，修正六經，三千之徒，並受其義。

translations.literal: Confucius inherited and transmitted the earlier age, revised the Six Classics, and three thousand disciples all received his teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius inherited and transmitted the earlier age, revised the Six Classics, and three thousand disciples all received his teaching.

sentences.zh: 至於戰國，孟軻、子思、荀卿之流，宗而師之，各有著述，發明其指。

translations.literal: By the Warring States period, Meng Ke, Zisi, Xun Qing, and others took them as their masters, each producing writings that developed their doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: By the Warring States period, Meng Ke, Zisi, Xun Qing, and others took them as masters, each producing writings that developed their doctrines.

sentences.zh: 所謂中庸之教，百王不易者也。

translations.literal: This is what is called the teaching of the Mean, unchanging through a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called the teaching of the Mean—unchanging through a hundred kings.

sentences.zh: 俗儒為之，不顧其本，苟欲嘩眾，多設問難，便辭巧說，亂其大體，致令學者難曉，故曰「博而寡要」。

translations.literal: When vulgar Confucians practice it, they disregard the root, wish only to stir the crowd, set up many difficult questions, use clever words and artful arguments, disorder the great framework, and make it hard for learners to understand—hence the saying, "Broad but without essentials."
translations.idiomatic: When vulgar Confucians practice it, they disregard the root, seek only to stir the crowd, set up many difficult questions, use clever words and artful arguments, disorder the great framework, and make it hard for learners to understand—hence the saying, "Broad but without essentials."

sentences.zh: :道者，蓋為萬物之奧，聖人之至賾也。

translations.literal: Daoists: the Way is the profundity of the myriad things and the utmost depth of the sage.
translations.idiomatic: Daoists: the Way is the profundity of the myriad things and the utmost depth of the sage.

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "The alternation of yin and yang is called the Way."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "The alternation of yin and yang is called the Way."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「仁者見之謂之仁，智者見之謂之智，百姓日用而不知。

translations.literal: It also says: "When the benevolent see it, they call it benevolence; when the wise see it, they call it wisdom; the common people use it every day without knowing it."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "When the benevolent see it, they call it benevolence; when the wise see it, they call it wisdom; the common people use it every day without knowing it."

translations.literal: Yin and yang are what we call Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang are what we call Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 天地變化，萬物蠢生，則有經營之跡。

translations.literal: When Heaven and Earth transform, the myriad things stir and are born, and then there are traces of ordering activity.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven and Earth transform, the myriad things stir and are born, and then there are traces of ordering activity.

sentences.zh: 至於道者，精微淳粹，而莫知其體。

translations.literal: As for the Way, it is subtle, pure, and refined, and no one knows its substance.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Way, it is subtle, pure, and refined, and no one knows its substance.

sentences.zh: 處陰與陰為一，在陽與陽不二。

translations.literal: Dwelling in yin, it is one with yin; dwelling in yang, it is not twofold with yang.
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in yin, it is one with yin; dwelling in yang, it is not twofold with yang.

sentences.zh: 仁者資道以成仁，道非仁之謂也；

translations.literal: The benevolent rely on the Way to complete benevolence—the Way is not what we call benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: The benevolent rely on the Way to complete benevolence—the Way is not what we call benevolence;

sentences.zh: 智者資道以為智，道非智之謂也；

translations.literal: the wise rely on the Way to achieve wisdom—the Way is not what we call wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: the wise rely on the Way to achieve wisdom—the Way is not what we call wisdom;

sentences.zh: 百姓資道而日用，而不知其用也。

translations.literal: the common people rely on the Way in daily use without knowing what they are using.
translations.idiomatic: the common people rely on the Way in daily use without knowing what they are using.

sentences.zh: 聖人體道成性，清虛自守，為而不恃，長而不宰，故能不勞聰明而人自化，不假修營而功自成。

translations.literal: The sage embodies the Way and completes his nature, keeps purity and emptiness, acts without presuming on his action, nurtures without dominating, and therefore can transform others without tiring his intelligence and accomplish his work without relying on deliberate effort.
translations.idiomatic: The sage embodies the Way and completes his nature, keeps to purity and emptiness, acts without presuming on his action, nurtures without dominating, and therefore can transform others without tiring his intelligence and accomplish his work without relying on deliberate effort.

translations.literal: Its mysterious virtue is deep and far-reaching, and its words and images cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: Its mysterious virtue is deep and far-reaching, and its words and images cannot be fathomed.

sentences.zh: 先王懼人之惑，置於方外，六經之義，是所罕言。

translations.literal: Former kings, fearing that people would be confused, placed it outside the canonical sphere; the meaning of the Six Classics is therefore rarely spoken of there.
translations.idiomatic: Former kings, fearing that people would be confused, placed it outside the canonical sphere; the meaning of the Six Classics is therefore rarely spoken of there.

sentences.zh: 《周官》九兩，其三曰師，蓋近之矣。

translations.literal: Among the Nine Categories of Bond in the Offices of Zhou, the third is called Teacher—this comes close to it.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Nine Categories of Bond in the Offices of Zhou, the third is called Teacher—this comes close to it.

sentences.zh: 然自黃帝以下，聖哲之士，所言道者，傳之其人，世無師說。

translations.literal: Yet from the Yellow Emperor downward, when sagely and wise men spoke of the Way, they transmitted it only to the right person, and the age had no masters who taught it publicly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Yellow Emperor downward, when sagely and wise men spoke of the Way, they transmitted it only to the right person, and the age had no masters who taught it publicly.

sentences.zh: 漢時，曹參始薦蓋公能言黃老，文帝宗之。

translations.literal: In Han times, Cao Can first recommended Master Gai, who could expound the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, and Emperor Wen took him as his model.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, Cao Can first recommended Master Gai, who could expound the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, and Emperor Wen took him as his model.

translations.literal: From this the transmission continued, and the study of the Way became numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From this the transmission continued, and the study of the Way became numerous.

sentences.zh: 下士為之，不推其本，苟以異俗為高，狂狷為尚，迂誕譎怪而失其真。

translations.literal: When inferior practitioners pursue it, they do not push to its root, but take being unlike the common custom as loftiness and being wild and narrow as excellence, becoming absurd, strange, and deceptive and losing the true Way.
translations.idiomatic: When inferior practitioners pursue it, they do not push to its root, but take being unlike the common custom as loftiness and being wild and narrow as excellence, becoming absurd, strange, and deceptive and losing the true Way.

translations.literal: School of Names: naming is what is used to set right the hundred things, arrange honor and baseness, rank noble and humble, each controlling a name and requiring the reality, with no mutual usurpation or excess.
translations.idiomatic: School of Names: naming is what is used to set right the hundred things, arrange honor and baseness, rank noble and humble, each controlling a name and requiring the reality, with no mutual usurpation or excess.

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：「古者名位不同，節文異數。

translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals says: "In antiquity names and ranks differed, and ritual forms and numbers varied."

sentences.zh: 」《孔子》曰：「名不正則言不順，言不順則事不成。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "When names are not correct, speech does not go forth; when speech does not go forth, affairs are not accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "When names are not correct, speech does not go forth; when speech does not go forth, affairs are not accomplished."

sentences.zh: 拘者為之，則苛察繳繞，滯於析辭而失大體。

translations.literal: When narrow practitioners pursue it, they are minute in scrutiny and tangled in analysis, stuck in parsing words and losing the great framework.
translations.idiomatic: When narrow practitioners pursue it, they are minute in scrutiny and tangled in analysis, stuck in parsing words and losing the great framework.

translations.literal: They exalt the conduct of Yao, Shun, and Yu of Xia—untrimmed thatch roofs, coarse millet food, paulownia coffins three inches thick, valuing frugality and universal love, honoring the father and elevating virtue, displaying filial piety to the world, revering ghosts and spirits while rejecting fate.

sentences.zh: :雜者，兼儒、墨之道，通眾家之意，以見王者之化，無所不冠者也。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous works: they combine the ways of Confucianism and Mohism, comprehend the intentions of the many schools, and thereby reveal the kingly transformation, encompassing all without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous works combine the ways of Confucianism and Mohism, take in the intentions of the many schools, and thereby show the kingly transformation that crowns all things.

sentences.zh: 古者司史曆記前言往行，禍福存亡之道。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Director of History systematically recorded former words and past conduct, and the ways of fortune and misfortune, survival and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Director of History kept systematic records of former words and past deeds, and of the paths of fortune and misfortune, survival and extinction.

sentences.zh: 然則雜者，蓋出史官之職也。

translations.literal: Thus miscellaneous works presumably arose from the duties of the historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: Thus miscellaneous works presumably grew out of the historiographer's office.

sentences.zh: 放者為之，不求其本，材少而多學，言非而博，是以雜錯漫羨，而無所指歸。

translations.literal: When unrestrained authors compose them, they do not seek the root; limited in talent yet wide in learning, their words miss the mark yet seem learned—hence they are jumbled and diffuse, with nothing to which they can be directed.
translations.idiomatic: When unrestrained authors write them, they do not pursue the root; scant in talent yet broad in learning, their words are off the mark yet seem erudite—so the result is a jumble without any clear direction.

translations.literal: The Changes says: "In antiquity they bent wood for bows and carved wood for arrows; the benefit of bow and arrow was to awe the world under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 然皆動之以仁，行之以義，故能誅暴靜亂，以濟百姓。

translations.literal: Yet all were moved by benevolence and enacted through righteousness, and thus could punish violence, still turmoil, and bring aid to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all were moved by benevolence and enacted through righteousness, and thus could punish violence, still turmoil, and bring aid to the common people.

sentences.zh: 下至三季，恣情逞欲，爭伐尋常，不撫其人，設變詐而滅仁義，至乃百姓離叛，以致於亂。

translations.literal: Down to the Three Ages of Decline, men indulged their passions and desires; warfare became commonplace. They did not comfort their people but devised schemes and deceit, extinguishing humaneness and righteousness, until the common folk turned away in rebellion and disorder followed.

sentences.zh: :天文者，所以察星辰之變，而參於政者也。

translations.literal: Astronomical works: they are what observe changes among the stars and relate them to government.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomical works are what observe changes among the stars and relate them to governance.

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Heaven displays portents, making fortune and disaster visible."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "Heaven displays portents, making fortune and disaster visible."

sentences.zh: 」《書》稱：「天視自我人視，天聽自我人聽。

translations.literal: The Documents states: "Heaven sees as my people see; Heaven hears as my people hear."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents states: "Heaven sees as my people see; Heaven hears as my people hear."

sentences.zh: 」故曰：「王政不修，謫見於天，日為之蝕。

translations.literal: Thus it is said: "If the king's governance is not cultivated, reproof appears in Heaven—a solar eclipse."
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is said: "If the king's governance is not cultivated, reproof appears in Heaven—a solar eclipse."

sentences.zh: 後德不修，謫見於天，月為之蝕。

translations.literal: If the queen's virtue is not cultivated, reproof appears in Heaven—a lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If the queen's virtue is not cultivated, reproof appears in Heaven—a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 」其餘孛彗飛流，見伏陵犯，各有其應。

translations.literal: As for comets, meteors, appearances and disappearances, transgressions and encroachments, each has its corresponding omen.
translations.idiomatic: As for comets, meteors, appearances and disappearances, transgressions and encroachments, each has its corresponding omen.

sentences.zh: 《周官》：馮相「掌十有二歲、十有二月、十有二辰、十日、二十有八星之位，辨其敘事，以會天位」是也。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou: the Heavenly Portent Officer "governs the positions of the twelve-year cycles, twelve months, twelve double-hours, ten days, and twenty-eight lodges, sorting affairs to align with heaven's positions"—this is what it means.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou: the Heavenly Portent Officer "governs the positions of the twelve-year cycles, twelve months, twelve double-hours, ten days, and twenty-eight lodges, sorting affairs to align with heaven's positions"—this is what it means.

sentences.zh: 小人為之，則指凶為吉，謂惡為善，是以數術錯亂而難明。

translations.literal: When petty men compose such works, they point to disaster as good fortune and call evil good, so numerological arts become confused and hard to clarify.

sentences.zh: :歷數者，所以揆天道，察昏明，以定時日，以處百事，以辨三統，以知厄會，吉隆終始，窮理盡性，而至於命者也。

translations.literal: Calendrical calculations: they are what gauge the Way of Heaven, examine dusk and dawn, fix days and times, arrange the hundred affairs, distinguish the three systems, know calamity and convergence, auspiciousness and misfortune, beginning and end, exhaust principle and fulfill nature, and thereby reach fate itself.

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Former kings regulated the calendar to clarify the times.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Former kings regulated the calendar to clarify the seasons.

sentences.zh: 」《書》敘：「期，三百有六旬有六日，以閏月定四時，成歲。

translations.literal: " The Documents narrates: "The cycle is three hundred and sixty-six days, using intercalary months to fix the four seasons and complete the year.
translations.idiomatic: " The Book of Documents narrates: "The cycle is three hundred and sixty-six days; intercalary months fix the four seasons and complete the year.

sentences.zh: 」《春秋傳》曰：「先王之正時也，履端於始，舉正於中，歸余於終。

translations.literal: " The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: "When former kings corrected the seasons, they began at the first month, took the middle as correct, and returned the remainder at the end.
translations.idiomatic: " The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: "When former kings corrected the seasons, they began at the first month, took the middle as correct, and returned the remainder at the end.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「閏以正時，時以序事，事以厚生，生民之道。

translations.literal: " It also says: "Intercalation corrects the seasons; seasons order affairs; affairs enrich life—this is the people's way.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "Intercalation corrects the seasons; seasons order affairs; affairs enrich life—this is the people's way.

translations.literal: " In the Offices of Zhou, this too was the duty of the Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Offices of Zhou, this too was the duty of the Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 小人為之，則壞大為小，削遠為近，是以道術破碎而難知。

translations.literal: When petty men pursue them, they make what is great into what is small and cut away the distant into the near, so the arts of the Way are broken into fragments and hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: When petty men pursue them, they make the great into the small and cut the distant into the near, so the arts of the Way are broken into fragments and hard to know.

sentences.zh: :五行者，金、木、水、火、土，五常之形氣者也。

translations.literal: : The Five Agents—metal, wood, water, fire, and earth—are the formative qi of the five constants.
translations.idiomatic: : The Five Agents—metal, wood, water, fire, and earth—are the formative qi of the five constants.

sentences.zh: 在天為五星，在人為五藏，在目為五色，在耳為五音，在口為五味，在鼻為五臭。

translations.literal: In heaven they are the five planets; in man the five viscera; in the eyes the five colors; in the ears the five tones; in the mouth the five flavors; in the nose the five odors.
translations.idiomatic: In heaven they are the five planets; in the human body the five viscera; in the eyes the five colors; in the ears the five tones; on the tongue the five flavors; in the nose the five odors.

sentences.zh: 在上則出氣施變，在下則養人不倦。

translations.literal: Above they issue qi and enact transformation; below they nourish mankind without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Above they send forth qi and work change; below they nourish mankind without wearying.

translations.literal: " Therefore the sages trace their beginning and end, penetrate the transformations of the numinous and bright, employ divination and stalk-casting to examine good and ill fortune, prognosticate the hundred affairs to observe what is to come, and observe form and method to distinguish noble from base.

sentences.zh: 右二百五十六部，合四千五百一十卷。

translations.literal: Above: 256 titles, 4,510 scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: Above: 256 titles, in 4,510 scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: :醫方者，所以除疾病，保性命之術者也。

translations.literal: : Medical prescriptions are the art by which diseases are removed and life and fate are preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The : Medical prescriptions are the art by which diseases are removed and life and fate are preserved.

sentences.zh: 天有陰陽風雨晦明之氣，人有喜怒哀樂好惡之情。

translations.literal: Heaven has the qi of yin and yang, wind and rain, darkness and brightness; man has the feelings of joy, anger, sorrow, delight, and love and hate.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has the qi of yin and yang, wind and rain, darkness and brightness; man has the feelings of joy, anger, sorrow, delight, love, and hate.

sentences.zh: 節而行之，則和平調理，專壹其情，則溺而生火。

translations.literal: When these are regulated and applied, harmony and balance prevail; when one feeling is indulged to excess, one is drowned and fire is born.
translations.idiomatic: When they are regulated and applied, harmony and balance prevail; when a single feeling is indulged to excess, one is drowned and fire is born.

sentences.zh: 是以聖人原血脈之本，因針石之用，假藥物之滋，調中養氣，通滯解結，而反之於素。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages traced the root of the blood and vessels, employed the uses of needle and stone, borrowed the nourishment of drugs, harmonized the center and nourished qi, cleared obstruction and released binding, and returned to the simple.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sages traced the root of blood and vessels, employed needle and stone, borrowed the nourishment of drugs, harmonized the center and nourished qi, cleared obstruction and released binding, and returned to the simple.

sentences.zh: 其善者，則原脈以知政，推疾以及國。

translations.literal: Those who excel at this examine the pulse to know governance, and extend illness to comprehend the state.
translations.idiomatic: Those who excel at this read the pulse to know governance, and extend illness to comprehend the state.

sentences.zh: 《周官》：醫師之職「掌聚諸藥物，凡有疾者治之」，是其事也。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou: the duty of the physician is "to gather all drugs and treat all who are ill"—such is the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou: the duty of the physician is "to gather all drugs and treat all who are ill"—such is the matter.

translations.literal: When the vulgar practice it, they turn back to the root and injure the nature.
translations.idiomatic: The when the vulgar practice it, they turn back to the root and injure the nature.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「有疾不治，恆得中醫。

translations.literal: Hence it is said: "To have illness and not treat it is often to obtain a middling physician.
translations.idiomatic: The hence it is said: "To have illness and not treat it is often to obtain a middling physician.

sentences.zh: 凡諸子，合八百五十二部，六千四百三十七部。

translations.literal: In all, the various masters comprise 852 titles and 6,437 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the various masters comprise 852 titles and 6,in 437 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 【結】《易》曰：「天下同歸而殊途，一致而百慮。

translations.literal: 【Conclusion】The Changes says: "Under heaven, all return by different paths yet arrive at the same end; a hundred thoughts lead to one consistency.
translations.idiomatic: The 【Conclusion】The Changes says: "Under heaven, all return by different paths yet arrive at the same end; a hundred thoughts lead to one consistency.

sentences.zh: 」儒、道、小說，聖人之教也，而有所偏。

translations.literal: " Confucianism, Daoism, and fiction are the teachings of sages, yet each is partial.
translations.idiomatic: The " Confucianism, Daoism, and fiction are the teachings of sages, yet each is partial.

sentences.zh: 兵及醫方，聖人之政也，所施各異。

translations.literal: Military writings and medical prescriptions are the governance of sages, yet each is applied differently.
translations.idiomatic: The military writings and medical prescriptions are the governance of sages, yet each is applied differently.

sentences.zh: 世之治也，列在眾職，下至衰亂，官失其守。

translations.literal: When the age is well governed, they are ranked among the many offices; when it declines into disorder, the offices lose their charge.
translations.idiomatic: The when the age is well governed, they are ranked among the many offices; when it declines into disorder, the offices lose their charge.

sentences.zh: 或以其業遊說諸侯，各崇所習，分鑣並騖。

translations.literal: Some then take their arts to persuade the feudal lords, each exalting what he has learned and setting off on separate paths at full gallop.
translations.idiomatic: The some then take their arts to persuade the feudal lords, each exalting what he has learned and setting off on separate paths at full gallop.

sentences.zh: 若使總而不遺，折之中道，亦可以興化致治者矣。

translations.literal: Yet if one could gather them without loss and break them back to the middle way, one could still use them to raise transformation and bring order.
translations.idiomatic: The yet if one could gather them without loss and break them back to the middle way, one could still use them to raise transformation and bring order.

sentences.zh: 《漢書》有《諸子》、《兵書》、《數術》、《方伎》之略，今合而敘之，為十四種，謂之子部。

translations.literal: The Book of Han has summaries of the Masters, Military Writings, Numerology, and Technical Arts; now they are combined and narrated together as fourteen categories, called the Masters section.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han has summaries of the Masters, Military Writings, Numerology, and Technical Arts; now they are combined and narrated together as fourteen categories, called the Masters section.
